scope: Existing valid rated, codified, normalized, rescue, bounded-comparison, and PI-report artifacts only.

direct_base_wage_value_signals.interpretation: The direct-value layer is quantitatively promising. It contains 533 fully normalized signals in the pre-rescue ledger, and rescue adds 10 full upgrades for an effective 543; another 168 are near-gap-ready. A direct-value signal does not itself establish schedule position or cross-occupation comparability.

explicit_schedule_tagged_spans.interpretation: Most explicit schedule-tagged spans are headings, fragments, or incomplete schedule references. Rescue adds one near-gap-ready schedule span but no full upgrade. The report must not treat 661 schedule tags as 661 comparison-ready schedules.

non_base_compensation_signals.interpretation: The non-base layer strongly supports a documentary mechanism claim. Rescue adds four near-gap-ready records but no full upgrades; it is not yet a quantitative total-compensation comparison layer.

candidate_summary.limit: Named-position comparison; duties, experience, schedules, job requirements, and hours equivalence remain unmatched.

bounded_comparison_support_now.claim_boundary: These are bounded local documentary position-rate statements. They do not support a final wage-gap estimate, cross-city average, national prevalence statement, regression, treatment effect, or causal claim.

position_and_schedule_location_comparabi.rule: Same municipality and overlapping effective period
position_and_schedule_location_comparabi.required_evidence: Both values must be operative in the same city and overlapping contract, fiscal, or calendar period. A broad document cycle cannot substitute for the actual rate window.
Compare base with base or the same identified non-base component with that component. Do not mix salary, maximum authorization, total compensation, overtime, stipend, allowance, or premium values.
Hourly-to-hourly or annual-to-annual is preferred. A conversion requires explicit work hours or a separately flagged and defensible assumption; source-reported values remain preserved.
Both records need explicit occupation/classification labels and a clear police, fire, or non-safety assignment. Broad department or town-wide headings are insufficient.
Match entry with entry, top with top, or the same tenure/step/grade/pay-band concept. A Year 1 officer may not be compared unqualified with an unlabeled or maximum non-safety rate.
Chief, captain, supervisor, specialist, and line-worker rates are not interchangeable. If rank/responsibility is unmatched, retain only a named-position documentary contrast.

Full-time, part-time, seasonal, temporary, salaried-exempt, and hourly/non-exempt positions require like-status pairing or an explicit limitation. Workweek/work-year differences must be known before annualization.
Confirm that an ordinance, schedule, award, or agreement was enacted, effective, and not merely proposed. Maximum ranges must be labeled as authorized maxima, not actual pay.

For the core design, identify each bargaining unit separately. A chief outside the unit, a town-wide ordinance line, or a discourse source may illustrate a local rate but does not become a matched unit-cycle row.

A base-wage pairing is incomplete for total-compensation interpretation unless longevity, shift, hazard, certification, uniform, overtime-related, stipend, and allowance components are either aligned or explicitly excluded.

report_repairs_required.safe_replacement: 2,687 direct base-wage/value signals, including 661 explicitly schedule-tagged spans; only six schedule-tagged spans are fully normalized in the current ledger.
report_repairs_required.reason: The 2,687 count is driven by base_wage_direct_value_strength, not a complete-schedule validator.

report_repairs_required.current_or_risky_language: Non-base compensation is a safety-specific channel
report_repairs_required.safe_replacement: Non-base compensation appears in both safety and non-safety records. Among side-resolved signals the evidence is safety-heavy, but more than half of the signal universe is side-unclear.
report_repairs_required.reason: There are 226 controlled non-safety signals, while 1,964 of 3,718 are side-unclear.

report_repairs_required.current_or_risky_language: The corpus shows the safety/non-safety non-base gap
report_repairs_required.safe_replacement: The current corpus documents non-base mechanisms on both sides, but it does not yet provide a matched total-compensation gap because component, period, and schedule-location alignment remain incomplete.
report_repairs_required.reason: Only 140 non-base signals are fully normalized, and no matched total-compensation estimator was run.

final_conclusions: Non-safety non-base examples exist and are source-grounded; the evidence is not safety-only.
The resolved non-base evidence is safety-heavy, but the 52.82% unclear-side share prevents a corpus-wide or prevalence conclusion.
Direct wage/value evidence is abundant, but the report must distinguish signals, schedule tags, fully normalized schedule rows, and comparison-ready matched records.
Current normalization supports mechanism descriptions and a small number of bounded position-rate examples, not a final safety/non-safety wage or total-compensation gap.
Position and schedule location—not municipality and year alone—must govern future pair construction.
